name: Keycloak Identity Hunt
author: Identity Security Team
prerequisites: Keycloak admin read-only access (view-realm, view-users roles)
Event log export enabled in realm settings
Realm name(s) documented and confirmed with system owner
required_tools: Keycloak Admin REST API (curl or Postman)
ELK Stack or Splunk with Keycloak event log index

hunt_actions.title: Authentication Anomaly Detection
actions: Pull failed login events exceeding threshold: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 'https://<keycloak>/admin/realms/<realm>/events?type=LOGIN_ERROR&max=1000' | jq '.[] | {time, ipAddress, details}'` — flag any username with > 10 failures in 60 minutes.

Identify service accounts using interactive browser sessions: In Keycloak Admin Console navigate to Realm > Events > Login Events. Filter by clientId matching known service clients (e.g., internal-api, backend-svc) and look for session_type=browser rather than expected service_account.

Detect password spray across accounts: Splunk query: `index=keycloak sourcetype=keycloak:events type=LOGIN_ERROR | bin _time span=10m | stats dc(userId) as unique_users count by _time, ipAddress | where unique_users > 20` — indicates spraying from single source IP.

Hunt for token refresh anomalies: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <admin_token>' 'https://<keycloak>/admin/realms/<realm>/sessions' | jq '.[] | select(.lastAccess < (.start + 60)) | {id, userId, ipAddress, lastAccess}'` — refresh tokens used well after session start without corresponding interactive use.

hunt_actions.title: Admin Privilege Escalation
actions: List all users with realm-admin or manage-users roles: `./kcadm.sh get-roles --target-realm <realm> --rolename realm-admin --users` and `./kcadm.sh get-roles --target-realm <realm> --rolename manage-users --users` — compare output against approved admin list.

Identify recent role mapping changes: In Keycloak Admin Console go to Realm > Events > Admin Events, filter Operation Type = CREATE or UPDATE, Resource Type = ROLE_MAPPING. Export and review all events within the hunt window.

Detect new identity providers added to realms: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 'https://<keycloak>/admin/realms/<realm>/identity-provider/instances' | jq '.[] | {alias, providerId, enabled, config.authorizationUrl}'` — compare against authorized IdP baseline.

Review client scope changes granting elevated permissions: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 'https://<keycloak>/admin/realms/<realm>/client-scopes' | jq '.[] | {id, name, protocol}' ` then for each scope: `curl .../client-scopes/<id>/scope-mappings/realm` and check for recently added realm-level roles.

hunt_actions.title: Session Hijacking Indicators
actions: Hunt for sessions where the IP address changed mid-session: Cross-reference Keycloak access event logs (type=CODE_TO_TOKEN and type=REFRESH_TOKEN) for the same sessionId but differing ipAddress. Splunk: `index=keycloak | stats values(ipAddress) as ips by sessionId | where mvcount(ips) > 1`

Identify offline tokens that have never been revoked: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 'https://<keycloak>/admin/realms/<realm>/sessions/offline' | jq '.[] | {id, userId, ipAddress, start, lastAccess}'` — flag sessions with lastAccess > 90 days and no revocation event.

Detect concurrent sessions from geographically disparate IPs: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' 'https://<keycloak>/admin/realms/<realm>/users/<userId>/sessions' | jq '.[]'` for high-value accounts — look for multiple active sessions with different geolocations active simultaneously within the same hour.

questions: What version of Keycloak (or Red Hat SSO) is currently deployed, and has it been patched to the latest security release within the last 90 days?
Are Keycloak admin and user event logs forwarded to the SIEM in real time, and are both LOGIN_ERROR and ADMIN event types captured?
How many realms are configured, which are classified as production, and is there a current architecture diagram documenting realm relationships?
Is brute-force protection enabled on all production realms with lockout thresholds documented and tested (Realm Settings > Security Defenses > Brute Force Detection)?
Which external identity providers are integrated (LDAP, Active Directory, SAML IdP, OIDC), and has each been reviewed for appropriate attribute mapping and scope restrictions?
Are offline tokens enabled for any client applications, and if so, what is the maximum offline session idle and max offline session lifespan configured?
Which accounts hold the realm-admin or manage-realm roles, and have those accounts been formally reviewed and recertified within the past 90 days?
Is the Keycloak administration console (/auth/admin) restricted to internal networks or VPN only, and is this enforced at the network layer (firewall/reverse proxy)?
